basic_information.official_title: AN ACT UPGRADING THE BULUAN DISTRICT HOSPITAL FROM LEVEL I DISTRICT HOSPITAL WITH SEVENTY-FIVE (75) BED CAPACITY TO LEVEL II DISTRICT HOSPITAL WITH ONE HUNDRED FIFTY (150) BED CAPACITY IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF BULUAN, PROVINCE OF MAGUINDANAO, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Converts the Buluan District Hospital in Maguindanao from Level I to Level II and doubles it from 75 beds to 150 — with both a three-year funding schedule and an immediate source of money for the first steps.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: To raise a district hospital to Level II standards and double its capacity, with the facilities, services and medical personnel increased to match.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Classification rises to Level II and beds double to 150. Facilities and professional services are upgraded commensurately and medical personnel correspondingly increased. Construction is placed under the direct supervision of the regional health ministry.
who_will_be_affected: Residents of Buluan and surrounding Maguindanao
Medical personnel, whose numbers are to be increased
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2022, with initial implementation directed into the Ministry's 2022 programme.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. Buluan District Hospital goes from 75 beds at Level I to 150 at Level II — and this act names where the first money comes from: the Contingent Funds.
in_practice: 75 beds becomes 150, and Level I becomes Level II
Facilities and professional services upgraded commensurate to the new size and classification
Budget apportioned in three tranches from 2022: 40% / 30% / 30%
Initial implementation to go into the Ministry's 2022 programme, chargeable to available Contingent Funds
Construction and upgrading under the direct supervision and control of MOH-BARMM

for_specific_groups.Patients: Level II care locally rather than a referral onward.
for_specific_groups.Medical staff: Section 2 requires the number of medical personnel to be correspondingly increased.
for_specific_groups.Anyone tracking delivery: This act is the most concrete of the cluster — a schedule and a named immediate funding source.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Initial implementation was directed into the Ministry's 2022 programme.
what_you_can_do: Ask MOH-BARMM what was charged to Contingent Funds for the initial implementation in 2022
Ask which tranche has been released and what it delivered
watch_out_for: The tranche percentages have no stated base amount.
Contingent Funds are 'available appropriations' — the act says funding may be charged there, not that it must.
No completion deadline for the works.

key_terms_explained.Level I / Level II hospital: Level I is basic emergency and general medicine; Level II adds specialist departments.
key_terms_explained.Contingent Fund: A reserve in the budget available for unforeseen or newly authorised spending.
key_terms_explained.Tranche: One instalment of a budget released in stages.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Dhu Al-Qa'dah 17, 1443 / 16 June 2022, approved by the Chief Minister on 12 July 2022.

benefits.headline: Level II care and 150 beds in Buluan, with money identified for the first steps.

direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Residents of Buluan and surrounding areas

indirect_benefits: A named immediate funding source, which most of these acts lack
limitations: Contingent Fund charging is permissive, not mandatory.

for_citizens: None. The act imposes no duty on the public.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Health – BARMM, which has direct supervision and control of the construction and upgrading
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A patient in Buluan needing a specialist service should find it locally once Level II status is delivered, rather than being referred to Cotabato City.
A resident asking when work starts can point to Section 5, which directed initial implementation into the Ministry's 2022 programme with funding chargeable to Contingent Funds.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Converts the Buluan District Hospital into a Level II District Hospital and increases bed capacity from 75 to 150, under the supervision and control of the Ministry of Health – BARMM.

Section 2 — Existing hospital facilities and professional health care services are upgraded and increased to conform with and be commensurate to the increase in bed capacity and classification level, and the number of medical personnel shall be correspondingly increased.

Section 3 — Personnel Services and Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses are included in the annual General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, apportioned in three tranches beginning in calendar year 2022: Year 1 – 40%, Year 2 – 30%, Year 3 – 30%.
Section 4 — Construction and upgrading of the hospital facilities and services is under the direct supervision and control of MOH-BARMM.

Section 5 — The Ministry of Health shall immediately include the initial implementation of the act in its 2022 programmes, the funding of which may be charged to available appropriations under the Contingent Funds, with subsequent funding included in the annual Bangsamoro Appropriations Act.
Section 8 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

impact.figures_note: Capacity doubles from 75 to 150 beds. Percentages are stated; the underlying amount is not.
